title: Measuring Learned Equivariance: An Information Theoretic Approach
abstract: arXiv:2610.17269v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Learning symmetries through data augmentation offers an alternative to architectural equivariance, but does not guarantee that a network respects those symmetries. Measuring learned equivariance is especially difficult for intermediate representations, whose group actions are not specified. In a finite discrete setting, we show that equivariance requires representations of original and transformed inputs to determine one another exactly, yielding a test based on normalized mutual information (NMI). For high-dimensional activations, we use centered kernel alignment (CKA) as a scalable test, with an exact guarantee for orthogonal feature transformations. Across architectures and tasks, augmentation usually increases transformation consistency, showing that learned equivariance can be probed directly from representations without recovering the hidden transformation rules that relate them.

translated_title: 测量学习到的等变性：一种信息论方法
translated_abstract: 通过数据增强学习对称性为架构层面的等变性提供了一种替代方案，但并不能保证网络真正遵循这些对称性。对于中间表示而言，测量学习到的等变性尤其困难，因为这些表示所对应的群作用并未被明确指定。在有限离散设定下，我们证明等变性要求原始输入与变换后输入的表示能够彼此精确确定，由此得到一种基于归一化互信息的检验方法。对于高维激活，我们采用中心化核对齐（CKA）作为可扩展的检验方法，并对正交特征变换给出了精确保证。在不同架构和任务上的实验表明，数据增强通常会提高变换一致性，这说明可以直接从表示中探测学习到的等变性，而无需恢复关联这些表示的隐藏变换规则。
tldr: 该论文提出基于归一化互信息（NMI）和中心化核对齐（CKA）的等变性检验方法，首次实现无需知晓隐藏变换规则即可直接从网络表示（包括中间表示）测量通过数据增强学习到的等变性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces equivariance tests based on normalized mutual information (NMI) for discrete settings and centered kernel alignment (CKA) for high-dimensional activations, enabling direct measurement of learned equivariance from representations—including intermediate ones—without recovering the hidden transformation rules.
